# The 5 best free keyword research tools in 2026

By Kiera Abbamonte · July 3, 2026

[](https://x.com/intent/post?url=https://zapier.com/blog/best-keyword-research-tool/ "Share article on X")[](https://www.linkedin.com/sharing/share-offsite?url=https://zapier.com/blog/best-keyword-research-tool/ "Share article on LinkedIn")[](https://www.reddit.com/submit?url=https://zapier.com/blog/best-keyword-research-tool/ "Share article on Reddit")

![Hero image with the logos of the best keyword research tools](https://images.ctfassets.net/lzny33ho1g45/5QQGTNrGhFhmSNSS76YBMe/f029e9079858b0c4874956a349908946/keyword-research-tools.jpg?fm=jpg&q=31&fit=thumb&w=1520&h=760)

_We independently review every app we recommend in our best apps lists. When you click some of the links on this page, we may earn a commission._ [_Learn more_](https://zapier.com/blog/affiliate-commission/)_._

There's no shortage of tools purpose-built for keyword research (literally hundreds of them), and they run the gamut from beginner-focused to highly advanced. They also range from totally basic and unhelpful to super valuable.

When done right, the best keyword research tools simplify and streamline your workflow—they make it easier to find the right keywords to target and give you the data you need to actually rank for them. But they shouldn't require you to empty out your bank account and sell your first-born child in order to access that data.

Improve your PPC management and performance

[Automate your campaigns](https://zapier.com/blog/improve-ppc-campaigns/)

After years of working with multiple clients who use all different tools for keyword research and [SEO](https://zapier.com/blog/seo-strategies/) content optimization, I've seen the best (and the worst) of them—and I know how important it is to choose the right keyword planner tool. To help, I considered more than 90 tools with a free option for keyword research. After in-depth testing, here are the five best free keyword research tools, including the all-around greats and apps built for more specific use cases.

Automate keyword research with Zapier

Connect your keyword research tool to the rest of your stack, and put insights to work automatically.

[Try Zapier](https://zapier.com/sign-up?utm_campaign=zpr-gbl-pgv-evr-blogsignupfullwidth-ctn&utm_medium=blog&utm_source=zapier)

## The best free keyword research tools

*   [Google Keyword Planner](https://zapier.com/blog/best-keyword-research-tool/#google) for researching paid keywords
    
*   [Semrush](https://zapier.com/blog/best-keyword-research-tool/#semrush) for advanced SEO professionals
    
*   [KWFinder](https://zapier.com/blog/best-keyword-research-tool/#kwfinder) for ad hoc keyword research
    
*   [AnswerThePublic](https://zapier.com/blog/best-keyword-research-tool/#answerthepublic) for content marketing
    
*   [Allintitle KW Explorer](https://zapier.com/blog/best-keyword-research-tool/#allintitle) for ad hoc keyword research beyond Google search
    

## What makes the best keyword research tool?

##### How we evaluate and test apps

Our best apps roundups are written by humans who've spent much of their careers using, testing, and writing about software. Unless explicitly stated, we spend dozens of hours researching and testing apps, using each app as it's intended to be used and evaluating it against the criteria we set for the category. We're never paid for placement in our articles from any app or for links to any site—we value the trust readers put in us to offer authentic evaluations of the categories and apps we review. For more details on our process, read the full rundown of [how we select apps to feature on the Zapier blog](https://zapier.com/blog/selecting-apps/).

The features that make for a great keyword research tool are pretty straightforward: you search for a given keyword, and the tool tells you about it. But there are so many different ways to _use_ keyword data, so I wanted to find tools that could handle a variety of use cases, along with a few designed for some of the most popular uses for keyword research.

During testing, I looked primarily at the factors below to determine which apps made the initial list.

*   **Data included.** The best keyword research tools give you all the data you need to rank for your chosen keyword. All of the apps I selected include, at minimum, traffic, keyword difficulty, and [competitive SERP analysis](https://zapier.com/blog/weaknesses-that-prevent-top-ranking-in-search-engine-results).
    
*   **Keyword optimization guidance.** You shouldn't have to be a 10-year SEO industry veteran to use keyword research tools—the best tools offer simple, straightforward suggestions to optimize for your keywords. There are tools (like [Ahrefs](https://zapier.com/blog/ahrefs-alternatives) and Moz) that do complete SEO analysis on your site, checking for everything from site speed and technical details to domain authority and topic clusters. That's not what we're looking for here. We're looking for tools that any business owner or marketer can use to quickly understand their target keyword and optimize their site to rank for it.
    
*   **Free plan allowances and upgrades.** Some tools include super limited results for free and call it a "free plan." Or they put time limits on the free plan, effectively making it more of a trial. I only included tools with evergreen free plans generous enough to actually be useful—and they won't break the bank when it's time to upgrade, either.
    
*   **Standalone functionality.** Since you're looking for something free, your keyword tool should be a one-stop shop—without requiring any additional tools or extensions to work for you, especially not ones you'd have to pay for. And while I didn't consider them for this roundup, there are a number of great [WordPress SEO plugins](https://zapier.com/blog/best-wordpress-seo-plugins/) you can start using right away if you have a WordPress site.

Have you ever wondered why local SEO is important for businesses? Local SEO is a process that helps to list your business higher in the local search results and increase brand awareness. It is important for businesses because it helps to improve the performance of a business in a local or specific area. Local keyword research is a crucial part of [local SEO](https://www.globalgenie.com.au/local-seo-services/) that helps you to understand how customers in your area search for products. You can list your business higher than others with the help of local keyword research. There are several tools that help in local keyword research for local SEO. ### Top 10 Best Local Keyword Research Tools For Local SEO in 2026

If you want to increase your business’s online visibility, then Semrush is one of the best tools that help you improve your online presence and reach the right audience. You can improve your keyword research process and [optimize the content](https://www.globalgenie.com.au/how-to-optimize-your-content-for-seo/) and structure of your website. Semrush gives users access to track their performance, analyze opportunities, and enhance their strategies.

#### Ahrefs

As a digital marketing tool, Ahrefs allows users to track rankings and identify keyword opportunities. Ahrefs has its web crawler that crawls the web like a search engine while gathering and processing the data to display this information in a user-friendly interface. It identifies the keywords that are currently ruling the local market and provides you with a dashboard that helps you to keep track of your data. 

#### Google Keyword Planner 

Google Keyword Planner is a well-established tool that is free and integrated within the Google Ads platform. It helps users find relevant keywords to improve their PPC campaign. This tool also provides you with the data on how often the customers search for specific terms and helps you discover new keywords. It also helps in building keyword research for search strategies to ensure the ads reach the targeted audience. 

#### Google Trends

Google Trends is a free tool that is provided by Google. It allows users to track the popularity of search queries in Google Search as well as which topic is ruling the local area. You can understand what people are currently looking for in the market, as well as customer behavior. It also helps you learn what is trending in the market and analyze customer preferences. This tool provides insights to optimize marketing strategies. 

#### Google Business Profile 

Google Business Profile is a tool that helps users create a strong online presence for their business. It allows you to manage how your business is shown on Google Search and Maps. 

Google Business Profile makes sure that your content is easily found on Google and the map. With the help of this tool, you can make changes to the information on your website and update things like your business name, address, phone number, products, and services. In this tool, customers can give you [reviews and ratings](https://www.globalgenie.com.au/how-to-increase-google-reviews/), and that can help build trust and authority with the customers. 

#### Ubersuggest

Ubersuggest is a free SEO tool that allows users to find new keywords and understand SEO difficulty. You can check how your website is ranking for a specific keyword with the help of UserSuggest. It also helps you identify SEO errors on your website and helps you improve the overall site’s performance. 

#### Localo 

Localo helps you improve the online visibility of your business and build a strong business profile on Google. It also helps businesses ensure their Google Business Profile has correct and accurate information like name, address, and phone number. Localo allows you to track the position of your business in the local search results and how those specific keywords are performing. 

#### Georanker 

Georanker is a local SEO tool that helps you track your business ranking in search results and improve your search engine optimization strategies. It also helps you to identify your competitor’s data and analyze opportunities for improvement. Georanker helps you understand which specific keyword is driving more traffic, and it also enables you to rank your business in different locations. 

#### Google Analytics

results.title: Edit your Business Profile - Google Business Profile Help
results.markdown:
Title: Edit your Business Profile - Google Business Profile Help

URL Source: https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617

Markdown Content:
You can edit your verified Business Profile on Google to keep your business info accurate and up to date. You can update details like your address, hours, contact info, and photos to help customers find and learn more about your business.

[Manage your business](https://business.google.com/?skipLandingPage=true&gmbsrc=ww-ww-et-gs-z-gmb-v-z-h~bhc-core-u|mybb)

**Important****:**

*   To show your business on Search, Maps, and other Google services, you must [add or claim your business](https://support.google.com/business/answer/2911778) then [verify your Business Profile](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7107242).
*   Some businesses might need to verify their Business Profile first before they can make any changes with their info.

## Edit a Business Profile

You can edit your Business Profile directly on Search or Maps. Certain features to manage your profile may differ between Search and Maps and your device's operating system.

**Important:** To edit your business info, you need to sign in to the Google Account that's linked to your Business Profile.

### [](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617)Edit your Business Profile on Google Search

1.   [Go to your Business Profile](https://business.google.com/).
2.   Select **Edit profile**.
3.   After you make your changes, select **Save**.

### Edit your Business Profile with the Google Maps app

1.   On your mobile device, open the Google Maps app ![Image 1: Maps](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/yBT9NcPCOum61BXUrmlfBecOpNufMGBDbh3rFQfIQu1Rs23tjRnhNdEou6yHAurnyw=h36).
2.   At the bottom right, tap **Business**.
3.   Tap **Edit profile**.
4.   After you make your changes, tap **Save**.

### [](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617)Suggest an edit to someone else's Business Profile

*   If you find something wrong with a Business Profile that you don’t own or manage, you can [suggest an edit](https://support.google.com/maps/answer/7084895).
*   If someone else's business is missing from Google Maps, you can [add a missing place](https://support.google.com/maps/answer/6320846).

## Review information collected by Google

**Important:**This feature is currently available for select regions, languages, and business categories and may not be available for all users.

To confirm your business details and keep your Business Profile updated and discoverable for customers looking for businesses like yours, Google may occasionally reach out using automated messages via call, text, or WhatsApp to the verified phone number on your profile.

Any information you provide in response to these messages may be used to update your profile. [Learn more about automated calls and texts from Google to confirm business info](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7690269).

To review and manage this collected information:

1.   [Go to your Business Profile](https://business.google.com/).
2.   Select **Edit profile**![Image 2: and then](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/LXIVMHxIoJ-ODytEi75yC-dtUFJFsRd6p8dopSSRr_ZUOPKvyuUgsU-7zVNA6ui8LmRz=h36)**Collected info**.
3.   Review the information to confirm its accuracy. 
    *   You can also find the source of this info and the date it was collected.
    *   This information displays in the language it was originally provided in.

4.   If you want to remove a piece of information, select **Delete**![Image 3: and then](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/LXIVMHxIoJ-ODytEi75yC-dtUFJFsRd6p8dopSSRr_ZUOPKvyuUgsU-7zVNA6ui8LmRz=h36)**Delete**. 
    *   **Tip:**Deleting collected information removes it from Google's records but does not change other details already on your Business Profile.

## [](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617)Types of edits

Here are some details and tips for the kind of info you can add or edit on your Business Profile.

[Business name](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617)

Enter your business name exactly as it appears on your real world business signage, stationery, and other branding. If you change your business name after it’s verified, you might need to verify your business again. [Learn more about Business Profile quality guidelines](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177).

[Category](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617)

Select the category that best matches what your business does. All locations of a business must share a “Primary category.” Choose a specific category that represents your main business. If you select several categories, the category in the first field will be your primary category. [Learn more about how to manage your business category](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7249669).

You can select up to 9 more categories. If you have trouble choosing a category for your business, choose one that’s general.

**Tips:**

*   Do not use categories solely as keywords or to describe features of your business.
*   Do not use categories that match other nearby or related businesses.  
**Example:**
    *   A business that’s located inside your business’s physical location
    *   Another business that your business is located inside.

[Address and pin location](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617)

[Service area](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617)

If your business serves customers within a specific local area, enter your service area. When you list your service area, this helps people know if you can visit or deliver to their location.

You can set your service area based on the cities, zip codes, or other places you serve. [Learn about how to set your service area](https://support.google.com/business/answer/9157481).

**Tip:** When you set your service area, be as specific and accurate as possible.

[Hours](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617)

*   To change your hours for holidays or other temporary periods, [set special hours](https://support.google.com/business/answer/6303076#holiday_hours).
*   If you have different hours for different features you offer, [set more hours](https://support.google.com/business/answer/9876800#more_hour).

[Phone number](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617)

In addition to your primary business phone number, you can enter up to 2 more phone numbers. They can be mobile numbers or landline, but not fax.

**Tip:** You can choose to hide your phone number on your Business Profile.

#### Hide your Business Profile phone number

results.title: Tips to improve your local ranking on Google
results.markdown:
Title: Tips to improve your local ranking on Google

URL Source: https://support.google.com/business/answer/7091

Markdown Content:
[Manage your business](https://business.google.com/?skipLandingPage=true&gmbsrc=ww-ww-et-gs-z-gmb-v-z-h~bhc-core-u|mybb)

When a customer searches for a business or place near their location, they’ll find local results on Google Maps and Search. For example, a customer might find local places near them if they search for “Italian restaurant” on their phone. Google tries to show customers the kind of nearby business they’d like to visit.

You can use your Business Profile to improve your business’s local ranking. [Learn more about how Google sources business information for search results](https://support.google.com/business/answer/2721884).

## Verify your business

## [](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7091)Keep your business information up-to-date

Businesses with complete and accurate info are more likely to show up in local search results. If your business info isn’t accurate, your Business Profile might not show up for relevant searches in your area.[Learn how to edit your Business Profile](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617).

Make sure your business info is as complete as possible in your Business Profile. This helps customers know what you do, where you are, and when they can visit. Provide information like:

*   Your full address, if your business has a location that customers can visit. [Learn how to manage your business address](https://support.google.com/business/answer/2853879).
*   Your business hours, including [special store hours](https://support.google.com/business/answer/6303076).[Learn how to edit your hours](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617#hours).
*   What kind of business you are.[Learn how to manage your business category](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7249669).
*   Other details such as parking or Wi-Fi availability. [Learn how to manage your business attributes](https://support.google.com/business/answer/9049526).

## [](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7091)Understand factors that determine local ranking

**Important:** There's no way to request or pay for a better local ranking on Google. We do our best to keep the search algorithm details confidential to make the ranking system as fair as possible for everyone.

Local results are mainly based on relevance, distance, and popularity. Together, these factors help Google find the best match for customers’ searches.

### Relevance

Relevance is how well a Business Profile matches what someone is searching for. To help Google better understand your business and match it to relevant searches, provide complete and detailed business info.

### Distance

Distance refers to how far each business is from the customer who’s searching. If a customer doesn’t share where they are, Google uses what it knows about their location.

### Prominence

Prominence means how well-known a business is. Prominent places are more likely to show up in search results. This factor’s also based on info like how many websites link to your business and how many reviews you have. More reviews and positive ratings can help your business’s local ranking.
